content:
I'll fully admit that my DIY iPhone camera mod looks ridiculous — but it's actually made using my iPhone for photos far more practical and enjoyable.

What started as a solution to a one-off filming problem has turned into something I find myself reaching for far more than I expected…

One of the biggest divides in the small camera world is whether or not to have a viewfinder. As an aside, old-school camera fans used to get really worked up about EVFs versus optical finders, but EVFs are now so good that few people care about this anymore.

Whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder has real practical benefits over using the rear screen for composition, especially when shooting in harsh sunlight. Even at maximum brightness, it's hard to see the screen properly in strong sun, and you can also get reflections on the display.

In London, this hasn't historically been a huge problem, but we've had record heatwaves this summer, and honestly I feel like the last time I saw a cloud or rain was about thirty years ago.

For me, though, it's about more than that. I find there's a difference in visual immersion — with a viewfinder you only see what's in the frame, whereas with the rear screen you're seeing the whole surrounding environment. Sometimes it's exactly this sense of immersion that makes me reach for a dedicated camera rather than my iPhone.

When I was choosing a camera for videography a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was an obvious frontrunner, but the lack of a viewfinder gave me pause. In the end I decided it wasn't a deal-breaker for me, because I'd mainly be using it indoors, and even when shooting outside, attaching a large monitor with a sun hood would solve most of the problem.

Sometimes, though, I want something a little more lightweight to operate than the whole rig with a monitor attached, so I found a simple accessory that's ideal for using outdoors. It's essentially a sun hood and magnifying loupe combo that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, giving you an optical viewfinder of sorts.

I had an upcoming shoot where I needed to record video with both the BMPCC 4K and my iPhone 16 Pro Max. I went to the location and did a quick test shoot, and the viewfinder accessory was a huge help. Since the BMPCC 4K and the iPhone have similar-sized screens, I wondered if the accessory would also work on my iPhone.

Of course the iPhone doesn't have a magnet array, but the iPhone is light enough that just holding it in place in front of the loupe with my hand works perfectly. I was pleasantly surprised at how well it worked, especially using the Camera Control button as a shutter.

I've since used the accessory in all sorts of situations to take photos, and whether it's being able to see the screen more easily in bright sunlight, or the sense of immersion, it's made the process far more enjoyable. My iPhone has long since become my primary camera, and with this DIY mod, I find myself reaching for just the phone in even more situations.

Genius or madness? Let me know your take in the comments. If you also think it's genius, unfortunately the specific product I bought appears to be discontinued, and I haven't yet seen anything similar designed for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, be sure to drop a link in the comments.
